sets.title: Plants Along the Trail
sets.description: Pressed leaves and wildflowers spotted on weekend hikes.
cards: *Plantago major*. Broad ribbed leaves flat to the ground, wind-pollinated spikes above.
A rosette of broad, strongly ribbed leaves with several flower spikes standing up out of it, growing where the grass runs out against the tarmac.
*Trifolium repens*. Creeping stems root at the nodes; heads brown from the base up.
One white clover head at full size, the lower florets already browning while the top ones are still fresh.
A complete dandelion seed head with every parachute still attached, lit against dark grass.

**Fern crozier**
- New fronds unroll from the base upward
- The coil protects the growing tip
- Ferns spread by spores, never seed
New fern fronds coming up beside a fallen branch, two still tightly curled and one part opened.
A close view of moss sporophytes, each capsule held clear of the cushion on a thin red stalk.
*Cichorium intybus*. Each flower opens for one morning and is closed again by midday.
A single chicory flower fully open, its pale blue rays square-cut and fringed at the tips.
Two views of the same plant: a closed green pod still on the stem, and a split pod letting its silk out.
*Digitalis purpurea*. Leaves in the first year, one tall spike in the second. Toxic throughout.
A foxglove with the lower bells open and the top of the spire still closed in bud.
Digitalis purpurea - Panoramic trail - Northern Black Forest 01.jpg
*Dactylorhiza*. A wet-meadow orchid; the spike opens from the bottom up.
A marsh orchid in flower with a fritillary butterfly settled on the spike, wings open.

**Monotropa uniflora**
- No chlorophyll, so it is white rather than green
- Feeds through fungi joined to tree roots
- Blackens as it goes over
A tight group of pale ghost pipe stems standing in leaf litter, the flower heads already blackening.
*Acer rubrum*. Red in the spring flowers, red in the autumn leaf, red in the twigs between.
One fallen maple leaf, still deep red, lying in a patch of light on the dark ground.
A spreading patch of wood sorrel over damp ground, with one small white flower open in it.

**Achillea millefolium**
- Flat-topped heads of many small florets
- Leaves finely divided, almost feathery
- Dry verges, meadows and roadsides
A flat-topped yarrow head in full flower, with a pale crab spider sitting among the florets.
*Crataegus monogyna*. One seed to a haw, which is where the *monogyna* comes from.
Hawthorn fruit part way to ripe, orange on one side and red on the other, hanging among the lobed leaves.

**Fagus sylvatica**
- Each husk holds two triangular nuts
- Heavy crops arrive only every few years
- A mast year feeds birds and mammals alike
Beech husks still shut on the branch, sitting among the leaves before they open and drop.
Cream meadowsweet plumes in full flower, held above the leaves on reddish stems.
*Dipsacus fullonum*. The dry heads stand all winter, and goldfinches work them for seed.
A dry teasel head with its spines intact and a tuft of fresh green growth pushing out of the top.

**Sorbus aucuparia**
- Pinnate leaves and berries in dense bunches
- Grows higher up a hill than most trees
- Thrushes and waxwings strip it bare
A cut rowan branch photographed against black, carrying a full cluster of red berries under its pinnate leaves.
*Orchis mascula*. One of the first orchids out, on chalk and in old woodland.
An early purple orchid in full flower, the hooded blooms working their way up the spike.
*Eryngium maritimum*. Waxy blue-grey leaves hold water on open shingle.
One low sea holly plant out among the shingle, with the beach running back to the dunes behind it.

sets.title: Pocket Geology
sets.description: Stones and minerals collected from riverbeds and roadcuts.
cards: Silicon dioxide, hardness 7. Six-sided prisms ending in a point, and hard enough to scratch glass.
A clear quartz crystal with its termination intact, photographed against black.
A clear quartz crystal with natural features.jpg
Coarse intrusive rock of quartz, feldspar and mica, cooled slowly well below the surface.
A rough granite block resting on paving, with the photographer's shadow falling across it.

**Slate**
- Mudstone recrystallised under pressure
- Splits along its cleavage, not its bedding
- The folding here came after the cleavage
Slate beds folded back on themselves in a coastal outcrop, the cleavage catching the light.
Contorted slate at Hayle Bay - geograph.org.uk - 629405.jpg
Fine-grained lava and the commonest rock of the ocean floor. Dark, dense and tough.
Rounded basalt cobbles packed across a shoreline, every one worked smooth by the surf.
Basalt cobble-boulder shoreline (Yaquina Head, Oregon, USA) 3.jpg
Cemented sand grains. The pink comes from iron oxide coating each grain.
A pink sandstone block with one fresh face, its bedding showing as faint parallel lines.
Weathering opens the grain of a rock face, and then frost and water carry the rest away.
A weathered rock surface at the water's edge, its banding worn down to faint pale streaks.
Quartz clouded pink by traces of titanium or manganese. It rarely forms good crystals.
A fist-sized piece of rose quartz, cloudy pink and translucent where it broke.

**Iron sulphide, FeS2**
- Grows in cubes with striated faces
- Brassy yellow, but much harder than gold
- Hardness 6, with a greenish black streak
Interlocking pyrite cubes with flat brassy faces and edges sharp enough to look machined.

**Trilobite**
- Marine arthropod, three lobes lengthwise
- Moulted its shell as it grew
- Cambrian to the end of the Permian
A trilobite in its matrix, the segmented thorax and tail standing clear in relief.
Purple quartz, coloured by iron and natural radiation. Heat turns it to yellow citrine.
Two halves of a geode opened out, both lined with small purple crystals over a white rim.
Microcrystalline silica formed inside chalk and limestone. Breaks with a curved face.
A slab of chert broken open, weathered pink along the top and fine grey inside.
High-grade metamorphic rock. Heat and pressure sorted its minerals into pale and dark bands.
A cut face of gneiss with pale and dark bands folded into a tight hook.
A worn piece of pumice, its whole surface full of the small cavities gas left behind.

**Mudstone**
- Silt and clay settled out in still water
- Splits along thin bedding planes
- Fossils survive best where the grain is finest
A blocky mudstone specimen on display, with the printed label naming the formation behind it.
Rounded pebbles cemented in a finer matrix. The rounding means water moved them first.
Rounded pebbles set in a coarse orange matrix, the block still carrying its catalogue number.
Calcium carbonate, hardness 3. It cleaves into rhombs and fizzes in dilute acid.
A honey-coloured calcite crystal, its cleavage faces meeting at the slanted angles that identify the mineral.

**Calcium fluoride**
- Cubes and octahedra, hardness 4
- Purple, green and colourless in one seam
- Many specimens glow under ultraviolet
Loose fluorite octahedra in purple and pale green, scattered among small brassy pyrite cubes.
A feldspar whose blue flash comes from light bouncing off layers inside the stone.
A rough labradorite block with one face polished, turned until the blue flash comes up.

**Copper carbonate**
- Forms where copper ore weathers
- Banding follows each growth surface
- Ground for green pigment for centuries
Polished malachite with light and dark green bands ringing several growth centres.
Faceting trades weight away for light returned through the table.
A faceted oval amethyst, pale violet, cut so the colour reads through the table.

sets.title: Records on My Shelf
sets.description: Records I return to, along with the sleeves, decks, and small parts around them.
cards: The colour is pigment in the PVC. It plays no differently from black vinyl.
A translucent blue seven-inch propped against its sleeve, lit from behind so the vinyl glows.
A twelve-inch LP runs at 33 rpm and holds around twenty minutes a side.
A record on the platter with the arm resting across it, and the mixer on a shelf above the deck.
Kazantip, Popovka, Crimea, Technics turntable, Vinyl turntable.jpg

**Groove**
- One continuous spiral, cut from the outside in
- The shape of the walls carries the stereo
- Lead-in and run-out hold no audio
A close black and white view across the grooves, with the light picking out every ridge.
Belt drive or direct, the platter has one job: hold a steady 33 or 45 rpm.
A turntable set up on a table with someone reaching past it, and an electric guitar on the wall behind.
Close-up of a dj reaching for a vinyl on the turntable, guitar in a blurry background.jpg
A plain black seven-inch with the centre knocked out, one tab of the spider still in place.
Slide a record out by its edges. Fingerprints on the playing surface collect dust.
A record halfway out of its sleeve, lifted beside a turntable with the lid standing open.
The stylus rides in the groove, and the counterweight sets how hard it presses.
A teal pressing on the platter with the cartridge down and the stylus in the groove.
Raking light shows the groove wall. Dust caught in it is most of what surface noise is.
A raking-light macro of the run-out grooves, close enough to show the dust on the surface.

**Sorting a collection**
- Sleeve and disc are graded separately
- The run-out carries the matrix number
- Play-grade anything you cannot hear first
Three collectors working through sleeves and loose discs spread out across a table.
Jaume Pujagut and his vinyl records sleeve collection.jpg
A seven-inch label carries credits the sleeve often leaves out.
The green label of a seven-inch single, its credits and rights notice set in small type around the edge.
Chi Mai 45 rpm vinyl single label detail.jpg
The large centre hole was cut for jukeboxes; an adapter fits it to a spindle.
A seven-inch label in teal and black, with the large centre hole punched clean out of it.
A plain white gatefold standing open on top of a deck, the embossed title catching the light.

**Direct drive**
- The motor turns the platter with no belt
- A pitch slider trims the speed
- Strobe marks show when it is on speed
A direct-drive deck from above in black and white, with the arm, the pitch slider and the platter edge all in frame.
A plastic disc that sits a seven-inch single flat on a full-size platter.
A plastic disc sold to sit a seven-inch single on a full-size platter, still bagged with the printed card it came with.

**Inner sleeve**
- Plain paper sheds fibres and scuffs
- Anti-static liners hold much less dust
- Store records upright, never in a stack
A record part way out of a plain paper inner sleeve, its label showing through the cut-out.
Bins are filed by genre and then by artist. The dividers do most of the work.
Full bins in a record shop, with hand-lettered genre signs on the wall above them.
A brush-and-pad cleaner resting on a record, ready to be drawn round the surface.

**Test pressing**
- Pressed in small numbers before the run
- Plain label, details filled in by hand
- Matrix numbers tie it back to the lacquer
A test pressing label with the date, title, artist and matrix numbers written into its printed blanks.
Run–D.M.C. - Faces-Back From Hell (test pressing single) (Side A).jpg
A picture disc laminates artwork inside the record, and usually plays noisier for it.
A plain black single lying beside a yellow picture disc, both out of their sleeves.
The cutter head writes one spiral groove into a lacquer master.
A record-cutting lathe with the cutter head over a blank disc and its controls along the front.

sets.title: Garden Birds
sets.description: Whatever lands on the feeder, catalogued from the kitchen window.
cards: *Erithacus rubecula*. Juveniles are spotted brown; the red front arrives with the moult.
A young robin still in spotted brown plumage, on bare ground, before the red breast comes through.
A blue tit seen from behind on a lichened branch, showing the blue wing and the long blue-grey tail.
*Carduelis carduelis*. A fine bill for teasing seed out of thistles and teasels.
A goldfinch on a hazel branch hung with catkins, its red face and gold wing bar clear.
*Aegithalos caudatus*. Travels in family parties and roosts in a huddle on cold nights.
A long-tailed tit on a bare branch, round-bodied with a tail longer than the rest of it.

**Troglodytes troglodytes**
- Among the smallest birds here, and the loudest
- Feeds low down, in cover
- The male builds several nests for the female to pick
A wren on a sawn log end, tail cocked, with the barring showing on its wings.
*Alcedo atthis*. Takes fish and larvae from a perch over water, and nests in a bank tunnel.
A female kingfisher on a bare log, holding a dragonfly larva across her bill.
*Passer domesticus*. The black bib marks a male, and grows broader with age.
A male house sparrow gripping a thin metal loop, with the black bib and chestnut wing markings clear.
A female blackbird low on the grass among fallen leaves, brown rather than black.
*Fringilla coelebs*. Double white wing bars; the male sings a set phrase with a flourish.
A male chaffinch on a lichened branch, its double white wing bars showing against the sky.

**Streptopelia decaocto**
- A narrow black half-collar on the nape
- Spread across Europe from the 1930s
- Breeds through most of the year
Two collared doves crowded onto a bracket against blue sky, one with its tail spread.
*Parus major*. The largest of the tits; the black stripe is broader on a male than a female.
A great tit in profile on a wooden perch, the black stripe running down its yellow breast.

**Sturnus vulgaris**
- Pale spots in winter, glossy green and purple in summer
- Walks rather than hops
- Mimics other birds, and machines
A starling on the lawn, its dark plumage flecked with pale spots and shot through with green.
*Columba palumbus*. The white neck patch separates it from stock dove and rock dove.
A wood pigeon settled on a wooden rail, the white patch on its neck turned to the camera.
*Sitta europaea*. The only bird here that climbs down a trunk head first.
A nuthatch working head-first down a tree trunk, which no other garden bird here does.
*Chloris chloris*. Yellow flashes in wing and tail, and a heavy bill for big seeds.
Two greenfinches on a concrete ledge, the yellow flashes on wing and tail catching the light.

**Turdus philomelos**
- Repeats each phrase two or three times
- Breaks snails open on a favoured stone
- Spotted breast, warm brown above
A song thrush standing on snow-covered grass, its spotted breast turned to the camera.
*Pyrrhula pyrrhula*. Black cap and stubby bill; quiet, and usually seen in pairs.
A bullfinch on a bare branch, with the black cap and short thick bill the species is known for.

**Dendrocopos major**
- A stiff tail props it against bark and mesh
- Drums in spring rather than singing
- Red on the nape marks the male
A great spotted woodpecker clinging to a hanging mesh feeder, with a log store behind it.
*Spinus spinus*. A small streaked finch; numbers rise here in hard winters.
A siskin on a branch in leaf and white blossom, its streaked yellow-green plumage showing.
*Strix aluco*. Roosts against a trunk by day and hunts small mammals at night.
A tawny owl roosting hard against a trunk, its plumage almost matching the bark behind it.

sets.creator: bex
sets.title: Film Cameras
sets.description: Film cameras from compact rangefinders to large folding field cameras.
cards: 1976. Shutter-priority SLR built around a microprocessor. FD mount, 50mm f/1.8 as standard.
A black AE-1 with the 50mm f/1.8 fitted, photographed square on against a plain ground.

**Pentax K1000, 1976**
- Fully mechanical; only the meter needs a battery
- K bayonet mount
- Sold for two decades as a first camera
A silver K1000 carrying a zoom far larger than the body, with the shutter dial and prism in view.

**Nikon F, 1959**
- Nikon's first system SLR
- Interchangeable prisms and focusing screens
- Built on the F bayonet mount, still in use
A silver Nikon F with a Nikkor lens fitted, the flat-topped prism giving it its familiar outline.
1954. Bayonet M mount, with rangefinder and viewfinder combined in one window.
A chrome M3 with a 5cm Summicron, its three front windows set across the top plate. Photographed at the German Museum of Technology in Berlin.
1972. A folding SLR that develops its print out in the light.
A folding SX-70 in brown leather and brightwork, opened out to its working shape.
1972. A small, quiet SLR with the shutter speeds on a ring around the mount.
A silver OM-1 on a table beside its lens cap, with the shutter-speed ring set around the lens mount.

**Minolta SR-T 101, 1966**
- Match-needle metering through the lens
- Mechanical shutter to 1/1000
- SR bayonet mount
A silver SRT-101 with a normal lens fitted and a second lens standing beside the body.

**Yashica Mat-124G, 1970**
- Twin-lens reflex for 120 and 220 film
- Twelve square frames to a roll of 120
- The waist-level hood folds flat
A Yashica twin-lens reflex with the finder hood closed, showing both lenses and the focusing knob.
A Retina opened for use, the lens standard carried out from the body on folding struts.
Twin-lens reflex: one lens views while the other exposes, so nothing blacks out.
The viewing and taking lenses of a Rolleiflex, with the focusing knob and shutter controls either side.

**Mamiya RB67**
- The back rotates, so the frame turns and the camera does not
- 6 by 7 cm negatives
- Bellows focusing, and heavy enough to want a tripod
An RB67 body from the front with no lens mounted, its waist-level finder folded up on top.

**Agfa Isolette**
- A folding camera for 120 roll film
- The bellows collapse it to pocket size
- Old bellows leak light along the folds
A folding Isolette opened out, the bellows drawn forward to carry the front standard.
1984. An amphibious camera sealed with O-rings and rated to 50 metres.
A Nikonos body and a wide lens laid out under warm light, both built to be sealed against water.
Modular 6 by 6: body, lens, finder and film magazine all come apart.
A 500C assembled with its normal lens and film magazine, standing on a wooden bench.
A gold Contax T2 in its lined presentation case, with two other compacts standing beside it.

**Linhof Technika**
- A folding technical camera for sheet film
- Rise, shift, swing and tilt on the front
- Rangefinder or ground glass
A Technika with its lens fitted and the leather focusing hood folded over to one side.
The American press camera: 4 by 5 sheet film, a folding bed and a flash bracket.
A press camera with its bed down and a large flash reflector mounted on the bracket beside it.

**Fuji GW690**
- Fixed 90mm lens, with no interchangeable mount
- Eight 6 by 9 cm frames to a roll
- A leaf shutter, so flash syncs at any speed
A fixed-lens rangefinder built around the 6 by 9 frame, with its cap and strap set down beside it.
The lens swings across a curved film gate for a 140 degree frame.
A Widelux with the back off, showing the curved film path the swinging lens sweeps across.
An 8 by 10 wooden field camera; every movement is in the standards.
A wooden field camera opened on its rail, bellows drawn out between the two standards.

sets.creator: kit
sets.title: Planets and Moons
sets.description: Every world out there that a spacecraft has sent back a decent portrait of.
cards: *SOHO, extreme ultraviolet.* A prominence stands clear of the disc.
The Sun imaged in extreme ultraviolet by SOHO, with a huge handle-shaped prominence held out above the limb in cooler, denser plasma.

**Closest in**
- Smaller than Ganymede or Titan, and still a planet
- Almost no atmosphere to move the heat around
- Craters everywhere, because nothing has erased them
A MESSENGER global view of Mercury, the sunlit face covered edge to edge with craters laid over craters.

**Under the cloud**
- Cloud hides the ground from any ordinary camera
- Magellan mapped the surface by radar instead
- The colour here was chosen, not photographed
A computer-built globe of the northern hemisphere of Venus, assembled from Magellan radar and coloured in the tan the mission chose for it.
*Blue Marble.* Four orbits of VIIRS data, stitched into one face.
The Suomi NPP Blue Marble composite, centred on North America, with Pacific cloud systems turning across the left of the disc.
*Clementine mosaic.* Fifty thousand frames, put together as one face.
A Clementine mosaic of the lunar nearside, the dark maria filling the middle of the disc and the rays of Tycho reaching up from the bottom.

**Global colour view**
- Polar caps of water ice and frozen carbon dioxide
- Dust storms that can close over the whole planet
- Two small moons, both irregular
A global colour view of Mars, the north polar cap bright at the top and the dark surface markings running in a band below it.
Phobos from about 5,800 kilometres, lit from one side, with its largest crater breaking the outline near the edge of the disc.

**Second heaviest in the belt**
- Dawn held orbit around it for a year
- Three craters in a row, called the snowman
- Pieces of it reach Earth as meteorites
A Dawn mosaic of Vesta, too small to have pulled itself round, with the three linked craters known as the snowman near the top.
*Occator crater.* The bright deposits are salts left by briny water.
The Dawn view into Occator crater on Ceres, built from a short exposure for the bright deposits and a normal one for the ground around them.
*Cassini, 2000.* The dark dot on the belt is the shadow of Europa.
A true-colour globe of Jupiter built from four Cassini frames, the Great Red Spot in the southern belts and the shadow of Europa falling on the cloud tops.
The most volcanic body we know of. It repaves itself faster than craters can form.
The Galileo view of Io, the whole disc mottled yellow and white by the sulphur compounds its volcanoes lay down.
*Galileo, reprocessed.* Ice crust, cracked through, ocean underneath.
A reprocessed Galileo colour view of Europa, the ice shell crossed in every direction by long reddish fractures.

**Largest moon in the system**
- Bigger than Mercury, and the only moon with a magnetic field
- Dark ground is old and cratered
- Pale ground is younger and grooved
A natural-colour Galileo view of Ganymede, the older dark terrain set against the paler, grooved ground that replaced it.
Every bright scar is an impact. Nothing has resurfaced it in billions of years.
The Galileo global view of Callisto, its dark surface covered in bright impact scars with no smooth ground anywhere on the disc.
*Cassini.* The rings are mostly water ice, and only metres thick.
Saturn from Cassini with the rings opened wide, the banding on the planet pale and soft-edged behind them.
*Natural colour.* Thick nitrogen air, and rain that falls as methane.
Titan passing in front of Saturn in natural colour, its haze layer giving the moon a soft orange edge against the bands of the planet.
Cassini approaching Enceladus, cratered ground across the top of the disc giving way to fractured, wrinkled terrain below it.
Voyager 2, 1986. The only visit anything has made, and almost no cloud to see.
Uranus from Voyager 2 in 1986, an almost featureless pale blue-green disc with no banding the camera could resolve.

**Voyager 2, 1989**
- The Great Dark Spot, with a bright companion cloud
- A fast white feature the team named Scooter
- Winds faster than anywhere else out here
Neptune from the last whole-planet frames Voyager 2 took, showing the Great Dark Spot with its bright companion and the streak called Scooter.
*Voyager 2, 1989.* Nitrogen ice, and geysers going off when it passed.
A Voyager 2 colour mosaic of Triton, the pink southern cap meeting darker, rougher ground along a ragged line.

sets.creator: wren
sets.title: Woodland Fungi
sets.description: Damp woodland, mostly from October onward, and mostly from turning things over.
cards:
**Amanita muscaria**
- The flecks are veil remains, and wash off
- Grows with birch and pine, never on its own
- Poisonous, and a long way from edible
A fly agaric in moss, the orange-red cap still domed and flecked with white above a thick white stem.

**Hypholoma fasciculare**
- Always in tight clumps on dead wood
- Gills turn green as the spores ripen
- Bitter enough that little will eat it
A tight clump of sulphur tuft on rotting wood and needle litter, the caps pale yellow and darker towards the middle.
*Trametes versicolor.* Banded brackets, in rosettes, on dead wood.
A rosette of turkey tail brackets on a cut log, each one banded in rings of brown, cream and rust.
Two shaggy inkcaps in rough grass, the caps still tall and scaled, before they start to blacken from the rim.
*Fomitopsis betulina.* Only on birch, and usually on a dying one.
A smooth pale bracket set against the dark trunk of a birch, its underside turned down towards the ground.
One common puffball on leaf litter, the head covered in short spines and the stem tapering away below it.

**Xylaria hypoxylon**
- White tips carry one kind of spore, the black base another
- Stays on the wood all winter
- Antler shapes, rarely more than a few centimetres
A line of candlesnuff along the cut end of a log, each one black at the base and white and forked at the tip.
Xylaria hypoxylon (candlestick fungus) location, Val Sinestra. 14-10-2024. (actm.) 01.jpg
*Daldinia concentrica.* Cut one across and it is ringed like a tree.
Hard rounded lumps of Daldinia under a fallen branch, brown where they are young and black where they are not.
Jelly ear on a fallen branch, the lobes folded over like an ear and translucent where the light comes through.
Bleeds red when it is cut, which is where the name comes from.
A beefsteak fungus on an oak trunk, one thick reddish-tan bracket pushing straight out of the bark.
*Laccaria amethystina.* Deep purple fresh, and it fades as it dries.
A single amethyst deceiver on a thin stem, the cap deep violet, standing clear of a soft green background.
Amethyst Deceiver - Laccaria amethystea - Violetter Lacktrichterling - Laccaria amethystina - 01.jpg
A scarlet elf cup open on the leaf litter, bright red inside and pale and felted around the rim.
GT Scarlet Elf Cup fungus - Sarcoscypha austriaca.jpg

**Lepista nuda**
- Lilac all through when young, fading with age
- Comes up late, often after the first frosts
- Edible, but only cooked
A wood blewit tipped over on leaf litter, showing the pale gills and the lilac wash running down the stem.
Clitocybe Nuda, AKA Lepista Nuda, AKA Wood Blewit.jpg
*Chlorociboria.* The wood stains green long before the cups show.
Weathered wood stained blue-green by Chlorociboria, with a few of the small cups open on the surface.

**Oudemansiella mucida**
- Nearly always on beech, well up the trunk
- The cap carries a slime that never dries
- Almost translucent while it is fresh
Porcelain fungus high on a mossy beech trunk, the caps white and glistening and thin enough to see light through.
Oudemansiella mucida, Porcelain Fungus, Enfield, UK.jpg
*Geastrum triplex.* The outer wall splits into rays and lifts the sac clear.
A collared earthstar opened on leaf litter, the rays folded back under a round spore sac sitting in its collar.
Collared Earthstar Geastrum triplex at Gunnersbury Triangle.JPG
Tiers of soft brackets straight out of the trunk, bright while young.
Overlapping brackets of Laetiporus stacked up a pale trunk, each shelf wavy-edged and darkening towards brown.
*Clavaria zollingeri.* Lilac fingers, unbranched, in old grassland.
A dense stand of violet coral among moss and fallen leaves, each lilac finger blunt at the tip.
Rises from a white egg, then opens red arms that smell of rot to draw flies.
Clathrus archeri just open on the forest floor, red arms lifting out of the white egg they grew from.
*Panellus stipticus.* It glows, faintly, and long exposures show it.
Panellus stipticus photographed in the dark on a fallen log, the gills giving off a steady green light.

sets.title: Fountain Pens, Old and New
sets.description: Fountain pens and nibs, from a boxed slide pen to a clear plastic Lamy.
cards: Made to stand in a desk holder, so they have no clip and a long tapered end.
Three black desk pens laid across a spiral notepad, two with gold nibs and one with steel.
Three patterned pens crossed on a wooden table: pale green, painted blocks of colour, and a dark blue check.
Aurora's piston filler, first made in Turin in 1947. This one has a matte black finish.
A matte black 88 clipped shut on a black leather notebook, gold trim at the band.
Made in Germany by Diplomat. This one has a 14 carat gold nib.
A dark blue Excellence uncapped beside an open bottle of blue ink, the lid set down next to it.

**Parker 51**
- Made from 1941 into the 1970s
- The hooded nib shows only its tip
- Aerometric filler from 1948
Parker 51s fanned out on pale paper in green, burgundy and grey, nibs pointing down.
Gold trim and a two-tone nib, plated in two colours for looks rather than writing.
A black pen with its cap resting behind it, a wide two-tone nib and gold bands at the section.
1932. Three pens from Osmia, a German maker, with patterned barrels.
Three Osmia pens stood on their ends for an advertising photograph, each throwing a long shadow.
Drie vulpennen van het merk Osmia, Bestanddeelnr 252-0963.jpg
Italian, from Delta near Naples. Orange resin with black and silver ends.
An orange Dolcevita uncapped on a dark desk, silver trim at both ends and a notebook behind.

**Pelican Pen No. 311**
